paragraphs: Online graph algorithms must make decisions as requests arrive, without knowing the full future input. Predictions can help, but evaluating their usefulness requires an error measure that handles both requests that were predicted but never arrive and requests that arrive unexpectedly. This paper proposes a general template that accommodates both, even when predicted and actual inputs have different sizes.

The measure uses a minimum-cost hyperedge cover in a specially constructed hypergraph. This gives the authors a way to connect discrepancies in predictions to algorithmic performance. They apply it to network design problems, including Steiner tree and facility location, and obtain more refined guarantees for the setting where requests are revealed in a list.

The paper also develops a framework for routing problems where transportation requests arrive over time, including traveling salesperson and dial-a-ride problems. Accurate predictions yield bounds better than established worst-case barriers. The tradeoff is a slight increase in worst-case bounds when predictions have arbitrary quality, making the benefit explicitly dependent on prediction accuracy.
neurips-2022-a-universal-error-measure-f.tldr: A general prediction-error measure supports improved online graph algorithms when predictions are accurate, with slightly worse worst-case bounds.

paragraphs: Deep networks have achieved strong empirical results, but explaining their data requirements remains difficult. The paper highlights a problem with existing analyses: beyond two layers, they often rely on counting parameters or produce sample requirements that grow exponentially with depth. Such bounds make it difficult to understand what additional depth actually costs in data.

The authors introduce an information-theoretic framework with its own definitions of regret and sample complexity. They use it to analyze learning when the data-generating process is a deep neural network. The two settings they study are deep ReLU networks and infinitely wide deep networks whose sum of weights is bounded.

Within this framework, they prove that sample complexity grows at most linearly with depth in the ReLU setting and at most quadratically in the infinitely wide setting. These are upper bounds under the specified data-generating processes. Their significance is that depth need not produce an exponential data requirement in this analysis, including a setting where counting a finite number of parameters is unavailable.
neurips-2022-an-information-theoretic-fr.tldr: An information-theoretic framework gives sample-complexity upper bounds that grow linearly or quadratically with depth for two neural data-generating settings.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning uses previously collected data to evaluate or improve decisions. This paper introduces a principle for approximating the Bellman equations, which express consistency between values and the rewards and future values they imply. Instead of enforcing those equations everywhere, the method enforces them along a user-selected space of test functions.

The authors use this principle for model-free learning with function approximation. It supports both confidence intervals for evaluating policies from data collected under other policies and optimization within a chosen policy class. Their policy-optimization guarantee compares the result against an arbitrary alternative policy through a tradeoff between that policy's value and its uncertainty.

Choosing different test-function spaces lets the same framework address different problems. The analysis also characterizes the efficiency lost when moving from on-policy to off-policy data and connects it to established measures of data coverage. For linear function approximation, the authors provide polynomial-time implementations with theoretical guarantees even without Bellman closure, a property concerning whether Bellman updates stay within the function class.
neurips-2022-bellman-residual-orthogonal.tldr: Testing Bellman consistency against selected functions enables offline policy evaluation and optimization with guarantees, including linear settings without Bellman closure.

paragraphs: In matrix completion and factorization, deep linear networks can favor low-rank solutions even without an explicit penalty demanding them. This preference comes partly from the optimization process itself. Prior work described in the abstract also links depth to an acceleration effect that strengthens this bias, raising the question of whether a simpler model could reproduce the benefit.

The paper proposes an explicit penalty designed to mirror that implicit preference. Its effect depends on pairing it with certain adaptive gradient optimizers, such as Adam. With this combination, a single-layer network can learn low-rank approximations whose generalization error is comparable to that of deep linear networks.

The single-layer approach also performs competitively with, or better than, several matrix-completion approaches across the tested parameter and data regimes. This supports removing depth for these learning settings when the penalty and optimizer work together appropriately. More broadly, the findings suggest that explicit regularization should be considered jointly with the optimizer's own preferences: the same penalty's usefulness can depend on how learning proceeds.
neurips-2022-combining-explicit-and-impl.tldr: An explicit penalty paired with suitable adaptive optimizers lets a single-layer model match deep linear networks' low-rank generalization in the studied settings.

paragraphs: Likelihood-to-evidence ratio estimation can be learned through classification, using either binary or multiclass objectives. The paper identifies a problem with the existing multiclass formulation, NRE-B: it contains an unknown intrinsic bias term. That term can make diagnostics unreliable even when the learned model otherwise provides useful information.

The authors propose a multiclass framework that is free of this particular bias at its optimum. It connects the earlier approaches by recovering binary NRE-A in one corner case and NRE-B in a limiting case. This provides a broader family of training choices while supporting diagnostics that depend on the ratio estimate's calibration.

The experiments compare methods under three data-availability regimes: unlimited joint draws, fixed data with unlimited prior draws, and fixed data and parameters. The strongest models occur at hyperparameter settings distant from those corresponding to the earlier methods, motivating different recommendations. The authors also suggest a mutual-information bound as a performance measure for simulation-based inference that does not require posterior samples, and provide experimental results.
neurips-2022-contrastive-neural-ratio-es.tldr: A broader multiclass ratio-estimation framework removes NRE-B's intrinsic bias at optimum and motivates new hyperparameter choices and diagnostics.

paragraphs: Tree-based models are widely used in settings where both interpretability and robustness matter, yet their certified robustness has received less attention than that of neural networks. This paper focuses on ensembles of decision stumps. Its goal is to establish guarantees about prediction robustness, alongside methods for improving those guarantees during training.

Smoothing evaluates a model under randomized inputs. For arbitrary models, that evaluation is typically approximate. The authors show that the structure of decision-stump ensembles permits exact and efficient evaluation through dynamic programming. This yields deterministic robustness certificates, including certificates that jointly cover numerical and categorical features.

The paper also derives a maximum-likelihood-optimal training method for smoothed stumps under randomization and introduces two boosting approaches aimed at improving provable robustness. Experiments on vision and tabular tasks report significantly higher certified accuracies than existing leading tree-based methods. The central contribution is therefore both computational and statistical: making smoothed predictions exactly evaluable for this model family and training ensembles that perform better under certification.
neurips-2022-de-randomized-smoothing-for.tldr: Decision-stump ensembles allow exact smoothing and deterministic robustness certificates, with training methods that improve certified accuracy on tested tasks.

paragraphs: Estimating causal parameters often requires first learning auxiliary regression or classification functions. Debiased machine learning makes it possible to use flexible estimators for those functions while retaining useful large-sample guarantees for the target parameter. Standard approaches typically fit the auxiliary functions on separate observations or use cross-fitting to separate the roles of the data.

This paper establishes a condition under which that separation is unnecessary. If the auxiliary learning algorithms satisfy suitable leave-one-out stability properties, the observations can be reused. The stability requirement concerns how the fitted procedure behaves when an individual observation is left out; it supplies the control needed to retain the inference guarantees.

The result preserves asymptotic normality and root-n consistency under the paper's conditions while allowing sample reuse, which can benefit moderately sized datasets. The authors also show that their proposed stability properties hold for bagged ensembles constructed by subsampling without replacement. This gives a concrete family of learning procedures to which the argument applies, rather than removing sample splitting for arbitrary auxiliary estimators.
neurips-2022-debiased-machine-learning-w.tldr: Suitable leave-one-out stability allows debiased machine learning to reuse samples while retaining asymptotic inference guarantees.

paragraphs: Understanding a task from first-person video requires more than recognizing individual actions. An agent must connect actions to changes in objects, understand why one step depends on another, and reason about goals. Multitasking and collaboration make this harder because activities overlap and each participant may see only part of what happens.

EgoTaskQA turns these aspects of task understanding into direct question-answering evaluations on real-world egocentric videos. Its questions cover action dependencies and effects, intentions and goals, and agents' beliefs about other agents. Four question types ask about current status, future events, causes, and hypothetical alternatives.

This design allows the benchmark to probe spatial, temporal, and causal understanding rather than relying only on action localization or future prediction as indirect indicators. The authors evaluate leading video-reasoning models and find substantial gaps relative to humans on complex goal-oriented videos. The benchmark's contribution is a structured way to identify what those systems understand about tasks and where their reasoning falls short.
neurips-2022-egotaskqa-understanding-hum.tldr: EgoTaskQA directly tests task reasoning in first-person videos and reveals substantial gaps between evaluated models and humans.

paragraphs: Few-shot meta-learning often emphasizes transferring knowledge across tasks. This paper instead focuses on generalization within a new task, where the handful of labeled examples may poorly represent the true data distribution. Minimizing loss only on those examples can therefore give a model too narrow a view of what the task contains.

The proposed approach assigns each training example a Gaussian-like surrounding distribution and derives a loss over these neighborhoods. It minimizes that vicinal loss instead of using only the observed examples. The derivation avoids exhaustively sampling all the surrounding points, making the distributional treatment usable without enumerating the whole neighborhood.

A key challenge is estimating each neighborhood's statistical parameters from very little labeled data. The method uses random walks starting from training examples and estimates weighted means and variances from the unlabeled data encountered. Experiments on four standard few-shot benchmarks report improvements over leading baselines. The findings support using unlabeled data to adapt the local training distribution for a particular task, alongside the broader benefits of meta-learning.
neurips-2022-improving-task-specific-gen.tldr: Adaptive neighborhoods estimated from unlabeled data improve task-specific few-shot learning by replacing pointwise empirical loss with vicinal loss.

paragraphs: Generalization bounds describe how performance on observed data relates to performance beyond it. PAC-Bayes analyses use a prior and posterior over hypotheses and typically measure their difference through KL divergence. This paper develops a PAC-Bayes-style bound that allows that comparison to use a range of integral probability metrics instead.

The authors give specific versions based on total variation and Wasserstein distance. A central feature is how the resulting guarantees change with the separation between prior and posterior. When they are far apart, the bounds recover the behavior of classical uniform convergence guarantees. When they are close, the bounds can improve.

This creates a connection between worst-case guarantees over a hypothesis space and guarantees sensitive to the algorithm and observed data. The contribution matters particularly for analyzing algorithms that operate in large hypothesis spaces: the bound can incorporate favorable information about the learned posterior rather than depending only on the broad space available. The improvement remains conditional on favorable prior-posterior proximity, not an unconditional tightening for every learning problem.
neurips-2022-integral-probability-metric.tldr: PAC-Bayes-style bounds using probability metrics interpolate between uniform convergence guarantees and improvements when prior and posterior are close.

paragraphs: The sound heard in a scene depends on both where it originates and where the listener stands. Neural Acoustic Fields represent this spatial relationship with a learned implicit function. The aim is to capture how a physical scene transforms sound, providing an auditory representation alongside the learned representations developed for visual scenes.

The method models acoustic propagation as a linear time-invariant system. Given an emitter location and a listener location, the network produces an impulse response describing the scene's acoustic effect for that pair. That response can then be applied to arbitrary sounds, separating the spatial propagation model from the particular sound being played.

Experiments on synthetic and real data show that the continuous representation can render acoustics for listeners at arbitrary locations. The authors also find that the learned representation can improve visual learning when only sparse views are available. Information about scene structure emerges during acoustic learning, suggesting that modeling how sound travels captures spatial properties useful beyond producing the sound itself.
neurips-2022-learning-neural-acoustic-fi.tldr: Neural Acoustic Fields learn location-dependent sound propagation and produce representations that can also aid visual learning from sparse views.

paragraphs: Neural text generators can repeatedly emit the same sentence when decoding favors the most probable continuation, as in greedy search. This is puzzling because consecutive sentence repetition is rare in human text. The paper investigates the problem by measuring how a sentence's previous repetitions affect the probability that the model will generate it again.

The experiments identify a reinforcing pattern: models favor repeating the previous sentence, and additional repetitions in the context raise the probability of another repetition. Sentences with higher initial probabilities usually exhibit stronger reinforcement. These findings explain how a locally attractive continuation can develop into a persistent sentence-level loop.

The proposed training method, DITTO, uses synthetic repetitive text to teach the model to reduce the probabilities of sentence repetitions. In experiments on open-ended generation with Wikitext-103 and summarization with CNN/DailyMail, it reduces repetition without sacrificing perplexity and improves generation quality. The results support addressing the learned reinforcement behavior during training, with benefits demonstrated across both tested generation tasks.
neurips-2022-learning-to-break-the-loop-.tldr: DITTO trains on synthetic repetition to counter self-reinforcing sentence loops, improving tested generation quality without sacrificing perplexity.

paragraphs: Tracking landmarks on articulated bodies usually requires substantial annotation, especially for animals without large labeled datasets. Multiple camera views can help detect errors and expand supervision, but established approaches depend on calibrated cameras and rigid geometry. Those requirements make casual recording and deployment in unconstrained settings difficult.

Multi-view Bootstrapping in the Wild combines a non-rigid 3D neural prior with deep flow to estimate landmarks from two or three uncalibrated handheld cameras. With annotations on only 1–2% of frames, the method produces 2D results reported as comparable to leading fully supervised approaches. It also produces 3D reconstructions that the authors report existing approaches cannot obtain in this setting.

The demonstrations include standard human datasets and casually captured zoo videos of several animal categories, including tigers, fish, chimpanzees, and flamingos. These results connect the reduced camera requirements to the annotation problem for less common categories. The authors release the code and a zoo dataset with 2D and 3D labels generated through minimal human intervention.
neurips-2022-mbw-multi-view-bootstrappin.tldr: MBW estimates 2D landmarks and 3D structure from a few annotations and two or three uncalibrated handheld cameras.

paragraphs: Meta-Album collects image-classification datasets to support research on learning from few examples, transferring knowledge, and learning across tasks. It contains 40 open datasets with verified licenses, each offering at least 20 classes and 40 examples per class. Its domains range from plants and animals to textures, vehicles, human actions, and character recognition.

The collection also spans different image scales, including microscopic imagery and remote sensing. All datasets are preprocessed, annotated, and placed in a common format. Three nested versions, Micro, Mini, and Extended, accommodate different computational resources, allowing researchers to work with a consistent collection at different scales.

The paper demonstrates few-shot learning uses for the first 30 datasets and describes the remaining 10 as forthcoming. It also presents a plan to expand the collection through competitions whose test data become public afterward, creating a rolling benchmark through OpenML. Code, baseline methods, data loaders, and contribution instructions support reuse. The contribution is a diverse, standardized research resource with an explicit mechanism for continued expansion.
neurips-2022-meta-album-multi-domain-met.tldr: Meta-Album standardizes diverse image datasets into scalable versions for few-shot learning, transfer learning, and an expanding benchmark.

paragraphs: A constrained Markov decision process asks an agent to achieve high reward while respecting a constraint. This paper determines near-optimal data requirements for learning such policies in discounted problems with access to a simulator. It distinguishes allowing small constraint violations from requiring the returned policy to satisfy the constraint exactly.

The authors develop a model-based algorithm for both settings. With relaxed feasibility, its sample complexity matches that of unconstrained MDPs, up to the factors hidden in the stated bound. With strict feasibility, the bound has a stronger dependence on the discount factor and also depends on a Slater constant describing the size of the feasible region.

A matching lower bound for strict feasibility shows that the additional difficulty is inherent to the setting, rather than just a weakness of the proposed algorithm. Together, the guarantees establish a statistical distinction between approximate and exact constraint satisfaction. Small permitted violations can leave the learning difficulty comparable to ordinary MDPs, whereas demanding zero violation carries an unavoidable additional cost under the studied simulator-access setting.
neurips-2022-near-optimal-sample-complex.tldr: Near-optimal bounds show that strict constraint satisfaction makes discounted MDP learning harder than allowing small violations.

paragraphs: Preference data often consists of a short ranked selection rather than a complete ordering of every available item. This paper studies participants who choose their k favorite items, in order, from a displayed candidate set. Different participants may see different sets, so the model must connect these partial observations to population-level preferences.

The authors introduce a distance-based ranking distribution resembling the Mallows model but using a new distance called Reverse Major Index. A central result concerns converting that full ranking distribution into probabilities for the choices people actually report. Although this aggregation involves all permutations, the resulting ranked-choice probabilities have simple closed-form expressions.

This makes the model useful for handling partial ranked selections without leaving their probabilities as an unwieldy sum over complete rankings. The paper develops methods for estimating the model's parameters and evaluates their generalization on real data. The reported strength is especially relevant when the observed data contains only a limited variety of candidate display sets, where learning preferences from restricted presentation patterns is important.
neurips-2022-on-a-mallows-type-model-for.tldr: A new ranking distance yields simple ranked-choice probabilities and supports preference estimation from varying candidate sets.

paragraphs: Different decision policies may have access to different observations and control different actions. The paper calls these differences mixed policy scopes. Combination therapy motivates the setting: different treatment regimens combine interventions and specify which information a physician can observe and which actions can be taken in context.

The authors study online reinforcement learning over such policy spaces and develop algorithms with sublinear regret relative to an optimal agent in the environment. Sublinear regret means that the accumulated performance gap grows more slowly than the number of interactions. The bound depends on the largest induced state-action space associated with the mixed scopes.

The paper also introduces a canonical representation for an arbitrary subset of intervention distributions specified through a causal diagram. This yields a nontrivial minimal representation of model parameters. Together, the contributions address both learning across policies with different observation and action scopes and representing the causal quantities involved. The treatment example motivates the mathematical setting; the stated findings concern algorithms, regret guarantees, and model representation.
neurips-2022-online-reinforcement-learni.tldr: Online learning algorithms achieve sublinear regret over policies with differing observation and action scopes, alongside a minimal causal parameter representation.

paragraphs: A navigation agent can struggle when obstacles or occlusions hide important parts of its surroundings from one camera. Combining several views offers more complete information, but sharing visual information also raises privacy concerns. This paper develops a framework that connects multiple cameras while restricting what participating parties can learn.

The method learns a multiview scene representation specifically for navigation. The authors provide a privacy guarantee that prevents a party from inferring information beyond the output task. The central idea is therefore to make information useful across camera views while limiting the information disclosed through the collaborative computation to the navigation task.

Experiments on a new navigation dataset show that these private multiparty representations support movement through complex scenes and around obstacles while preserving privacy. The framework also accommodates an arbitrary number of camera viewpoints. These contributions bring together two requirements that arise in shared perception: using complementary observations to navigate and formally controlling what the participating parties can infer. The abstract describes public release of the dataset as planned.
neurips-2022-private-multiparty-percepti.tldr: A multiview navigation framework combines camera information with a proof that parties cannot infer information beyond the output task.

paragraphs: The paper studies quantum optimization when a function is close to convex but need not itself be convex. Its assumption is precise: over a convex feasible set in n dimensions, the target function differs everywhere from some convex function by at most epsilon divided by n. Under this condition, the algorithm finds a point within epsilon of the target function's minimum.

The algorithm uses roughly cubic-in-n quantum evaluation queries, with logarithmic factors suppressed, giving a polynomial improvement over the best-known classical algorithms. Its construction combines a quantum simulated-annealing framework with a quantum version of the hit-and-run walk. The speedup is stated in quantum query complexity.

The authors also apply the approach to zeroth-order stochastic convex bandits. They obtain regret scaling as n to the fifth power times the square of log T, again suppressing logarithmic factors, compared with a classical lower bound growing as the square root of T. This improvement in time dependence comes from a quadratic quantum improvement in mean estimation's multiplicative error.
neurips-2022-quantum-speedups-of-optimiz.tldr: Quantum algorithms speed up approximately convex optimization and achieve polylogarithmic-in-time regret for the studied stochastic convex bandit setting.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised learning combines labeled and unlabeled examples, but commonly assumes that every class appears in the labeled set. When unlabeled data includes additional classes, those examples can be assigned incorrectly to known classes. The resulting confusion can damage performance on both the previously labeled classes and the unseen ones.

This paper proposes a method with two components. The first uses pairwise similarity between examples to enable classification of unseen classes. The second coordinates the learning pace for seen and unseen classes through an adaptive threshold with distribution alignment. This addresses both the absence of labels for some classes and the imbalance in how the two groups are learned.

The reported experiments show significant improvements for both seen and unseen classes compared with previous studies. The contribution is a semi-supervised approach that explicitly accommodates classes absent from the labeled data, rather than forcing all examples into the known categories. Its two-part design reflects the finding that recognizing unseen classes and coordinating their learning with known classes are related needs.
neurips-2022-robust-semi-supervised-lear.tldr: Pairwise similarity and synchronized learning improve semi-supervised classification when unlabeled data contains classes absent from the labeled set.

paragraphs: Graph clustering seeks groups of nodes using both their connections and any descriptive features attached to them. Existing neural approaches can learn representations that are useful in general without making clusters easy to recover. They may also become impractical on very large graphs. S3GC is designed to address both concerns.

The method combines contrastive learning, graph neural networks, and node features to produce representations intended for clustering. Its experiments show that the combination can recover the correct cluster structure even when graph connections alone or node features alone do not provide enough information. This demonstrates a benefit from combining the two information sources in the tested settings.

Across a variety of benchmarks, the authors report better clustering results than leading methods, including gains of as much as 5% in normalized mutual information. They also report scalability to graphs of size 100M. The stated contribution joins cluster-oriented representation learning with large-scale operation, rather than treating the quality of the learned features and the scale of the graph as separate objectives.
neurips-2022-s3gc-scalable-self-supervis.tldr: S3GC learns clusterable graph representations by combining connections and node features, with strong benchmark results and scalability to graphs of size 100M.

paragraphs: A model's explanation is useful to people only if its reasons make sense to them. This paper calls the degree of human agreement with those reasons human precision. SELOR aims to integrate explanations into a deep model while preserving prediction performance, so users can understand its decisions and collaborate with it.

The framework uses logic rules to support both prediction and explanation. The authors argue that these rules can express useful predictive reasoning while aligning with human judgments about reasons. SELOR does not require a predefined collection of rules or human annotations, and it can be trained differentiably using widely used deep-learning components.

Experiments report explanations closer to human decision logic than those from other methods while maintaining the underlying deep model's performance. The result supports treating explanation as part of the model's reasoning process rather than as an unrelated output. Its stated success concerns agreement with human reasoning and preserved predictive performance; human precision specifically measures agreement with explanations, giving that goal a clear meaning within the framework.
neurips-2022-self-explaining-deep-models.tldr: SELOR integrates learned logic-rule reasoning into deep models, improving agreement with human explanations while maintaining prediction performance.

paragraphs: In repeated multiplayer games, learning rules can be judged by swap regret: how much a player could have gained by systematically replacing its chosen actions with other actions. This paper develops efficient, uncoupled learning dynamics with logarithmic swap regret when every player follows the proposed procedure in a general-sum game.

The guarantee improves the previously best bound from the fourth power of log T to log T. The method also retains an optimal square-root-of-T swap-regret guarantee in the adversarial regime. These are distinct guarantees: the faster rate depends on all players using the dynamics, while the adversarial guarantee covers the more demanding setting.

The construction combines optimistic regularized learning with self-concordant barriers. A key proof shows that, with a time-invariant learning rate and all players following the method, second-order path lengths grow only logarithmically. This controls how the dynamics evolve and supports the regret result. The authors also present a simpler analysis that avoids a previously used higher-order smoothness framework, and suggest that the path-length property could have further applications.
neurips-2022-uncoupled-learning-dynamics.tldr: Efficient uncoupled dynamics achieve logarithmic swap regret when all players use them and retain optimal square-root regret against adversarial play.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization involves an outer problem whose solution depends on solving an inner problem. Popular methods AID-BiO and ITD-BiO contain subproblems that can receive either many iterations or only a few. Spending more effort inside each update makes that update more expensive, but may reduce the total work needed to converge.

The paper develops unified convergence analyses covering the loop choices for both optimizers, then derives computational complexity comparisons. For AID-BiO, iterating to estimate the inner optimum improves overall efficiency despite increasing the cost of each update. A separate loop for approximating a Hessian-inverse-vector product reduces gradient complexity.

For ITD-BiO, the two loops occur together. The upper and lower convergence bounds show that these loops are necessary for a vanishing convergence error in the analyzed setting; the no-loop implementation has an unavoidable error that does not vanish. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical findings. The practical message is that reducing work per update can sacrifice either overall efficiency or attainable convergence, depending on the optimizer.
neurips-2022-will-bilevel-optimizers-ben.tldr: Unified analyses show that loops improve AID-BiO's efficiency and are necessary for vanishing convergence error in the studied ITD-BiO setting.

paragraphs: Compressing transformer models to binary or ternary precision can make them smaller enough for resource-constrained devices, but preserving accuracy is challenging. Existing approaches often rely on complicated, expensive distillation pipelines and extensive tuning. This paper examines whether that complexity is needed, including for smaller transformers already compressed through distillation.

The authors systematically study important hyperparameters and training strategies from earlier approaches. They find that previous ultra-low-precision baselines were substantially under-trained. Based on these findings, they develop a simpler extreme-compression pipeline, connecting the choice of training procedure to how well aggressively compressed models perform.

The resulting pipeline can omit pretraining knowledge distillation when producing a five-layer BERT and still outperform earlier leading methods such as TinyBERT in the reported comparisons. Combining extreme quantization with layer reduction gives a 50-fold model-size reduction and new leading results on GLUE tasks. The findings show that training adequacy materially affects compression comparisons and that a simplified pipeline can deliver strong results under the studied settings.
neurips-2022-xtc-extreme-compression-for.tldr: A systematic training study leads to a simpler transformer-compression pipeline with 50-fold size reduction and strong GLUE results.
